text.p: Swiss shares continued Friday's consolidation, slipping below 4,500 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) on profit taking.
Activity picked up near the end of the session after Wall Street moved into positive terrain, but volumes were low as insecurity about further developments prevailed.
The SMI ended down 59.3 points, or 1.13 percent, at 4,463.2 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index fell 34.24 points, or 1.19 percent, to 2,837.0.

The development of the U.S. dollar, U.S. economic data on Tuesday and Thursday as well as Federal Reserve board chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony before Congress may give the market direction, one trader noted.
"The flow of funds may have come to an end until it is clear where we are going," he said.
Pharmaceuticals Novartis and Roche, which had been sought in the past few sessions, were hit by profit-taking.

Most-active Novartis bearer shares fell 33 francs to 1,759. Trade in the rights issues for Novartis unit Ciba Specialty Chemicals will start on Wednesday and this could have an impact on Novartis' shares, one trader said.
Nestle gave up 15 francs to close at 1,601.
Among financials, UBS slipped 18 francs to 1,280. Credit Suisse fell 2.50 francs to 152. Insurer Zurich traded unchanged at 426.50 francs. Baloise rose 15 francs to end at 2,905.
ABB slipped three francs to 1,808. The company's 1996 data are due for release on Thursday.
Electrowatt slid eight francs to 531 after news of its plans to pay a dividend of eight francs per share.
